questions.question: What does IEEE 802.11 define?
questions.explanation: IEEE 802.11 is the standard that defines wireless LAN technology, commonly known as WiFi.

questions.question: Which frequency band does 802.11b use?
questions.explanation: 802.11b operates in the 2.4 GHz frequency band with speeds up to 11 Mbps.

questions.question: Which 802.11 standard operates exclusively in the 5 GHz band?
questions.explanation: 802.11a operates only in the 5 GHz band, offering less interference but shorter range.

questions.question: What does SSID stand for?
questions.explanation: SSID is the network name that identifies a specific wireless network.

questions.question: Which wireless security protocol is most secure?
questions.explanation: WPA3 is the latest and most secure WiFi security protocol with enhanced encryption.

questions.question: What access method does 802.11 use to avoid collisions?
questions.explanation: CSMA/CA is used in wireless networks to avoid collisions before they occur.

questions.question: Which 802.11 standard supports both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz?
questions.explanation: 802.11n operates on both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands for flexibility and performance.

questions.question: What is the maximum theoretical speed of 802.11g?
questions.explanation: 802.11g operates at 2.4 GHz with a maximum speed of 54 Mbps.

questions.question: What mode allows wireless devices to communicate without an access point?
questions.explanation: Ad hoc mode enables direct device-to-device communication without a central access point.

questions.question: Which wireless standard is also known as WiFi 6?
questions.explanation: 802.11ax, branded as WiFi 6, offers improved speed and efficiency in congested areas.

questions.question: Which frequency band typically provides longer range and better wall penetration?
questions.explanation: Lower frequencies propagate farther and penetrate obstacles better than higher bands.

questions.question: How many non-overlapping channels exist in the 2.4 GHz band?
questions.explanation: Only channels 1, 6, and 11 are non-overlapping in the 2.4 GHz band.

questions.question: What process maps RF coverage and interference before deploying access points?
questions.explanation: A wireless site survey identifies coverage gaps, interference, and optimal AP placement.

questions.question: Which wireless security protocol is deprecated because of its weak RC4 implementation?
questions.explanation: WEP's small initialization vectors and flawed RC4 usage make it trivially crackable.

questions.question: Which encryption algorithm does WPA2 use?
questions.explanation: WPA2 uses AES with CCMP for strong encryption of wireless traffic.

questions.question: Which encryption protocol did the original WPA use before AES?
questions.explanation: WPA used TKIP as a transitional fix for WEP's weaknesses before WPA2's AES-CCMP.

questions.question: Which 802.11 standard first introduced MIMO?
questions.explanation: 802.11n introduced MIMO, enabling multiple simultaneous spatial streams.

questions.question: What technology allows an access point to transmit to multiple clients simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Multi-User MIMO serves multiple clients on the same channel at the same time.

questions.question: What attack uses a rogue access point mimicking a legitimate network to lure clients?
questions.explanation: An evil twin AP impersonates a legitimate SSID to intercept client traffic.

questions.question: What is the practice of searching for wireless networks while moving through an area?
questions.explanation: War driving maps discoverable wireless networks from a vehicle or on foot.

questions.question: Which 802.11 standard, known as WiFi 5, operates only in the 5 GHz band?
questions.explanation: 802.11ac (WiFi 5) uses wide channels and MU-MIMO exclusively in 5 GHz.

questions.question: What does WPA3 use instead of PSK to resist offline dictionary attacks?
questions.explanation: Simultaneous Authentication of Equals provides forward secrecy in WPA3-Personal.

questions.question: Which antenna type focuses signal strength in one direction?
questions.explanation: Directional antennas concentrate RF energy toward a target area for longer range.

questions.question: What problem occurs when two clients reach the access point but cannot hear each other?
questions.explanation: Hidden nodes cannot sense each other's transmissions, causing collisions at the AP.

questions.question: Which mechanism mitigates the hidden node problem by reserving the medium?
questions.explanation: RTS/CTS handshakes reserve the channel so hidden nodes defer transmission.

questions.question: What unit expresses wireless transmit power relative to one milliwatt?
questions.explanation: dBm measures absolute power referenced to 1 milliwatt; dBi measures antenna gain.
